note: Behavior-trace evals for loom's session skills. Each prompt is answered by an agent that READS the skill files and traces the flow — the skills themselves mutate real machine state (ledgers, artifacts, git pushes), so evals verify the text produces the intended behavior unambiguously rather than executing a live run. The only live eval is --dry-run, which writes nothing by design.

evals.prompt: Trace /loom:harvest (no arguments) in a git repo with 3 eligible non-active sessions and 1 active session. List: every point where the user is prompted, the order sessions are processed, when each ledger write and watermark advance happens, and what scope artifacts land at.
evals.expected_output: Zero prompts (cap question only fires >12). Sessions processed oldest→newest, active last. One §K.7 write per session combining the analyzed[] entry AND the watermark advance; active session folded but never ledgered/watermarked. All artifacts at project scope (user scope only outside a git repo; never plugin).

evals.prompt: Trace /loom:harvest --review over 2 eligible sessions where the user selects nothing for session 1 and one usage for session 2. What happens after the zero-selection?
evals.expected_output: Session 1 is ledgered and the loop CONTINUES to session 2 (no stop, no re-ask). Session 2 runs cards + multi-select + scope question + per-update diff-confirm, then applies. Watermark advances after each session.

evals.prompt: Trace /loom:harvest --dry-run. What is written to disk?
evals.expected_output: Nothing: no lock, no $cfg/loom/ init, no agents, no ledger mutation, no report. Discovery list + eligibility + cap outcome presented, then stop.

evals.prompt: Trace /loom:harvest <session-id> for an old session of the current project. Is it interactive, and does the watermark move?
evals.expected_output: Fully interactive (cards + multi-select + scope + diff-confirm). One analyzed[] entry ledgered; the watermark NEVER moves in single mode.

evals.prompt: Trace /loom:learn mentor with 3 unanalyzed sessions. When does expert review run, when are items implemented, how many publishes happen, and when do ledger writes occur?
evals.expected_output: Per session (oldest first): one analysis agent → §H review (usually ONE reviewer; trio only for hooks/settings/multi-artifact sets) → APPROVE items implemented automatically → a git COMMIT of that session's delta (no bump, no push) → one §K.7 write (entry + watermark), commit strictly before the ledger write. Interactive batch publishes exactly once after the loop iff ≥1 session committed anything — one bump covering all three commits, which ride along in the push.

evals.prompt: Trace /loom:harvest --headless and /loom:learn mentor --headless with 15 eligible sessions each. Does AskUserQuestion ever fire, and what happens to the active session in harvest?
evals.expected_output: AskUserQuestion never fires on any path: harvest's cap auto-defaults to Newest 12 (remainders ledgered skipped-cap); learn --headless takes exactly ONE session (the oldest eligible) with no cap question and no skipped-cap entries — the other 14 stay eligible by watermark and lastRun.remaining=14 tells the runner to fire again; publish is deferred until the fire that drains the queue. NO_TRANSCRIPTS/dead-ends stop cleanly with a message. Harvest skips the active session entirely (it is the headless runner itself). --headless overrides --review.

evals.prompt: In a project-wide auto harvest, session 3 is a fork/resume copy of session 1 and proposes an identical artifact. What happens?
evals.expected_output: The artifact already exists (created from session 1), so test -e routes it as an update; the effective diff is empty → no-op skip, recorded in the report. No duplicate artifact.

evals.prompt: In a project-wide auto harvest, the analysis agent for session 2 crashes. What happens to the run and to session 2 on the next run?
evals.expected_output: Session 2 is ledgered outcome=error and the loop continues with session 3. On the next run, error is re-eligible (§K.3 rule 1) so session 2 is retried.

evals.prompt: Machine has two config dirs: ~/.claude and ~/.claude-ntb, each with loom automation configured. Trace /loom:automate setup run with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/.claude-ntb, where a legacy shared-label com.loom.daily.plist exists pointing at ~/.claude-ntb, plus a com.loom.daily.plist.bak.* backup, and ~/.claude has no live schedule. List every file and launchctl operation and the end state of BOTH installs.
evals.expected_output: New plist com.loom.daily.claude-ntb.plist written and loaded with PATH and CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/.claude-ntb baked in; legacy plist detected as this install's (runner-path grep) so unloaded and deleted, and its .bak.* files removed with it; the runner is installed via temp + mv (never in-place cp), preceded by the run.lock in-flight guard. Nothing under ~/.claude or any ~/.claude-labelled schedule is read or modified.

evals.prompt: Both com.loom.daily.claude.plist and com.loom.daily.claude-ntb.plist are installed. Trace /loom:automate --status and then --stop, run with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR unset (i.e. ~/.claude). What exactly is matched, reported, and removed?
evals.expected_output: --status computes slug=claude and checks liveness with an ANCHORED match (launchctl list | awk NF3 | grep -qxF com.loom.daily.claude) so the claude-ntb job can never satisfy it via prefix match; it reports only ~/.claude's schedule, config, stamp and log tail, writing nothing. --stop checks run.lock first, then unloads/deletes only com.loom.daily.claude.plist; the claude-ntb plist, config, ledgers and stamps are untouched and the report says config.json was kept.

evals.prompt: During a /loom:harvest --headless run fired by the daily automation under CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/.claude-ntb, in a project directory that is NOT a git repo, harvest decides to create a user-scope skill and a user-scope memory file. State the exact paths written, per the artifact catalog.
evals.expected_output: All user-scope paths resolve through ${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}: the skill lands at ~/.claude-ntb/skills/<name>/SKILL.md and the memory at ~/.claude-ntb/memory/<topic>.md with its index line appended to ~/.claude-ntb/MEMORY.md. Nothing is written under ~/.claude — a literal ~/.claude path is the pre-isolation bug.

evals.prompt: Trace a daily-run.sh fire where config.json has notify.email set, harvest succeeds, learn disposes 2 sessions and publishes, but the Gmail connector is disabled so the daily-report fire fails. When does the email step run, where does its failure land, and does the day stamp?
evals.expected_output: After the learn phase (including its publish), the runner fires /loom:daily-report --headless exactly once, watchdogged like any fire, cwd = the marketplace repo. The failure lands ONLY in stamps/fail-notify-<date> (FAIL_MARK is rebound in a subshell around the notify fire; the skill also self-reports soft failures there); the day's own fail-<date> stays absent, so the run still stamps last-ok and exits 0, logging 'daily report email FAILED'. Nothing retries until the next fire.

evals.prompt: Trace /loom:daily-report --headless fired manually twice: once when config.json exists but notify.email is absent, once when notify.email is set but no run happened today (no daily-<date>.log). What is sent and what is written in each case?
evals.expected_output: Both are clean skips: a log-friendly line (no notify.email configured / no run on <date> — nothing to report), no email attempt, and NO fail-notify marker — markers are written only on a genuine headless compose-or-send failure. --dry-run likewise never sends and never writes a marker.
